days.title: Mercies new every morning
days.summary: Jeremiah wrote of God's new mercies while sitting among the ruins of Jerusalem. God's compassion is not a store that runs low; it is renewed every morning. Begin the new year by trusting His faithfulness for today.

days.title: Seeking the kingdom first
days.summary: Jesus told anxious listeners to seek God's kingdom and righteousness first. When God comes first, every other need finds its proper place. Put Him at the top of your plans this year and trust Him with the rest.

days.title: Seeking God with your whole heart
days.summary: God promised the exiles in Babylon that they would find Him when they searched with all their heart. He is not hiding, but He invites a wholehearted search. Bring Him your full attention today and trust the promise that you will find Him.

days.title: The one thing worth desiring
days.summary: David, a king with every reason to ask for power, said his one desire was to dwell near God and behold His beauty. One great desire brings order to all the smaller ones. Make nearness to God the center of your life today.

days.title: A soul that thirsts for God
days.summary: In the dry wilderness, David compared his longing for God to physical thirst. The soul has a need that only God can satisfy. Seek Him early today and let Him refresh your dry places.

days.title: Found by those who seek
days.summary: Moses told Israel that even if they were scattered far away, they could seek God from there and find Him. God does not require us to fix everything before we return. Seek Him today from right where you are.

days.title: A heart that longs for God
days.summary: The psalmist compared his longing for God to a deer searching for water in a dry land. Spiritual longing is often a sign of living faith, not failing faith. Bring your thirst honestly to God today and let Him refresh you.

days.title: A mind stayed on God
days.summary: Isaiah promised perfect peace to the one whose mind is stayed, or leaning, on God. Peace does not come from the absence of trouble but from trust anchored in Him. When your thoughts begin to spin today, bring them back to Him.

days.title: Leaving the past behind
days.summary: Paul, who had both failures and successes in his past, chose to forget what was behind and reach for what was ahead. Neither old guilt nor old victories should steer our future. Give your past to God today and lean forward into what He has prepared.

days.title: Pressing toward the mark
days.summary: Paul described his life as a runner pressing toward the finish line. The prize was God's high calling in Christ, worth every effort. Live on purpose today and take a step toward what God is calling you to.

days.title: God does a new thing
days.summary: God told His people to stop looking only at past wonders because He was doing a new thing. He promised a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. Watch today for the new thing God may already be doing in your life.

days.title: Numbering our days wisely
days.summary: Moses, who had seen a generation pass, asked God to teach him to number his days. An honest view of life's shortness leads to a wiser heart. Ask God to help you spend today on what truly lasts.

days.title: Committing your work to God
days.summary: Proverbs tells us to commit, or roll, our works onto the Lord. When we bring our plans to Him, our thoughts become settled and steady. Before today's work begins, place it in God's hands.

days.title: Committing your way to the Lord
days.summary: David, looking back on a long life, urged us to commit our whole way to the Lord and trust Him. Committing without trusting means taking the load back again. Hand God the direction of your life today and rest in His promise to act.

days.title: Delighting in the Lord
days.summary: Psalm 37:4 invites us to delight in the Lord, promising that He will give us the desires of our heart. As we delight in Him, our desires are reshaped to match His. Look for a reason to enjoy God today.

days.title: Rising early to pray
days.summary: After a long day of healing and teaching, Jesus rose before dawn to pray alone. Time with the Father was the source of His strength, not an extra activity. Find a quiet place today and meet with God before the day's demands begin.

days.title: Morning prayer
days.summary: David brought his prayers to God in the morning and then looked up, expecting an answer. Prayer becomes richer when we watch for God's response. Pray with expectation today and look for His hand at work.

days.title: Pressing on to know the Lord
days.summary: Hosea called people who treated God casually to keep pressing on to know Him. God's coming is as certain as the sunrise and as refreshing as the rain. Keep pursuing a deeper knowledge of God today.

days.title: Time to seek the Lord
days.summary: Hosea urged God's people to break up their fallow ground, soil left hard from neglect. Hearts can also harden when spiritual things are neglected. Today is the time to seek the Lord and prepare your heart for His rain.

days.title: Seek God and live
days.summary: Amos spoke to a nation busy with religion but far from God, calling them to seek God Himself. God wants a relationship, not just activity. Seek Him personally today and find the life He promises.

days.title: Seeking meekness and righteousness
days.summary: Zephaniah called the meek to seek the Lord, along with righteousness and meekness. Humility is never finished; it must be pursued again and again. Ask God today to make you gentle, upright, and close to Him.

days.title: Seeking His face continually
days.summary: In David's song of celebration, the people were urged to seek the Lord, His strength, and His face continually. Seeking God is not occasional but a lifestyle of turning toward Him. Look for moments throughout today to turn your heart toward His presence.

days.title: Humble hearts that seek His face
days.summary: God told Solomon that when His people humble themselves, pray, seek His face, and turn from wickedness, He will hear, forgive, and heal. Renewal begins with God's own people looking honestly at themselves. Take the first step of humility before God today.

days.title: Never forsaken by God
days.summary: David wrote that those who know God's name will trust Him, because He never forsakes those who seek Him. Knowing God's character is the foundation of trusting Him. Get to know Him better today, and let your trust grow.

days.title: No good thing lacking
days.summary: David noted that even strong young lions go hungry, but those who seek the Lord will not lack any good thing. Our provision comes from God, not our own strength. Seek Him today and trust Him to supply what is truly good.

days.title: Choosing the good part
days.summary: While Martha was busy serving, Mary sat at Jesus' feet, and Jesus said she had chosen the good part. Good activities can crowd out the best thing, which is time with Him. Make a choice today to sit at His feet and listen.

days.title: Ask, seek and knock
days.summary: Jesus taught His followers to ask, seek, and knock in prayer, words that grow in intensity. Persistent prayer is not nagging an unwilling God; it is trusting a loving Father. Pick up a prayer you may have set down and keep knocking today.

days.title: Seeking things above
days.summary: Paul urged believers who had been raised with Christ to seek the things above, where Christ reigns. Earthly matters are real but not ultimate. Let heaven's priorities shape your choices today.

days.title: Setting your mind on heaven
days.summary: Paul told believers to set their minds and affections on things above rather than things on earth. Our thoughts steer our lives toward whatever we love most. Choose today to set your mind on God and His goodness.

days.title: Seeking with the whole heart
days.summary: The psalmist sought God with his whole heart, yet still asked God to keep him from wandering. Even sincere seekers need God's help to stay on the path. Pray today for a heart that seeks Him and stays close to His Word.

days.title: The Lord always before me
days.summary: David set the Lord always before him, and because God was at his right hand, he would not be moved. Keeping God in view brings stability when life pushes against us. Carry this habit into the rest of the year.

days.title: A friend who loves at all times
days.summary: Proverbs describes a friend who loves at all times and a brother born for hard seasons. True friendship is revealed when life becomes difficult. Thank God for faithful friends today, and be one to someone who is struggling.

days.title: A friend closer than a brother
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that people who want friends must show themselves friendly. It also speaks of a friend who sticks closer than a brother. Take a step of friendliness today, and rest in God's faithful presence.

days.title: Two are better than one
days.summary: Solomon observed that two people working together accomplish more and enjoy more than one working alone. God designed us for partnership, not isolation. Look for a way to share a task or come alongside someone today.

days.title: Lifting a fallen friend
days.summary: Solomon pictured two companions where one lifts the other up after a fall. Those who fall alone have no one to help them rise. Be the friend who reaches out a hand today.

days.title: Loyal love that stays
days.summary: When Naomi had nothing left to offer, Ruth chose to stay with her and follow her God. Loyal love stays when leaving would be easier. Show that kind of faithful love to someone today.

days.title: Hearts knit in friendship
days.summary: Jonathan's soul was knit with David's, and he loved him as his own soul. Though he could have seen David as a rival, he chose selfless friendship. Thank God for close friends today and ask Him to make you a faithful friend.

days.title: Iron sharpens iron
days.summary: Just as iron sharpens iron, friends sharpen one another. Growth sometimes involves friction, but it makes us better. Seek friends who help you grow, and be that kind of friend to others today.

days.title: The honest words of a friend
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that honest words from a friend are better than the flattery of an enemy. Loving truth may sting, but it helps us grow. Receive honest counsel with grace today, and speak the truth in love when needed.

days.title: Called friends of Jesus
days.summary: Jesus told His disciples that He no longer called them servants but friends, because He had shared the Father's words with them. Every believer is invited into that same friendship. Talk with Jesus today as a trusted friend.

days.title: Kindly affection for one another
days.summary: Paul urged believers to show warm family affection and to compete in honouring one another. This runs against our instinct to seek recognition for ourselves. Look for a way to honour someone else today.

days.title: Rejoicing and weeping together
days.summary: Paul calls us to rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. Both require humility and love that enters into another's experience. Share someone's joy or sorrow today with your whole heart.

days.title: Bearing one another's burdens
days.summary: Paul calls believers to bear one another's burdens, which fulfils the law of Christ. Carrying someone's load is love in action, just as Christ carried ours. Ask God to show you someone you can help today.

days.title: Love that is patient and kind
days.summary: Paul describes love as patient and kind, without envy, boasting, or pride. These qualities heal relationships while their opposites poison them. Choose patience and active kindness toward someone today.

days.title: The power of a soft answer
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that a gentle answer turns away anger, while harsh words stir it up. Answering softly takes strength, not weakness. Choose a gentle response today when tension rises.

days.title: Love that keeps no score
days.summary: Paul writes that love is not rude, selfish, easily provoked, or quick to assume evil. It does not keep a record of wrongs. Let go of a grudge today and choose to think the best of someone.

days.title: Bearing with one another in love
days.summary: Paul urged believers to live with humility, gentleness, and patience, bearing with one another in love. Others have flaws, and so do we. Ask God today for grace to bear patiently with someone who tests you.

days.title: Love that binds us together
days.summary: Paul describes love as the garment that binds all the other virtues together. Without love, kindness and patience can become cold. Choose to put on love deliberately today.

days.title: Training up a child
days.summary: Proverbs encourages training a child in the right way, so that the path remains when they are grown. Children learn more from example than words. Pray for the young people in your life today and model the way they should go.

days.title: Honouring father and mother
days.summary: The fifth commandment calls us to honour our father and mother, and it carries a promise. Honour means giving weight and respect, even when parents are imperfect. Find a way to honour your parents, or give thanks for them, today.

days.title: Parents who build up
days.summary: Paul told fathers not to provoke their children but to nurture and instruct them in the Lord. Authority is given to build others up, not to crush them. Ask today whether your leadership nurtures those in your care.

days.title: Children are a gift from God
days.summary: Psalm 127 calls children a heritage and reward from the Lord. They are gifts entrusted to us, not possessions we own. Thank God for the children in your life and treat them as treasures today.

days.title: The goodness of unity
days.summary: Psalm 133 celebrates how good and pleasant it is when people live together in unity. Unity is not sameness but being joined by something greater than our differences. Ask God how you can help build unity today.

days.title: As for me and my house
days.summary: At the end of his life, Joshua challenged Israel to choose whom they would serve and declared that his household would serve the Lord. Every home faces that choice, again and again. Decide today what will be at the center of your household.

days.title: The law of kindness
days.summary: The woman in Proverbs 31 speaks with wisdom, and kindness is the law of her tongue. Our words shape the atmosphere of our homes. Let kindness govern how you speak today.

days.title: Kindness for a friend's sake
days.summary: David sought out Jonathan's son Mephibosheth and showed him kindness for his father's sake. He restored his land and gave him a seat at the king's table. Show undeserved kindness to someone today, just as God has shown it to you.

days.title: Building one another up
days.summary: Paul urged suffering believers to comfort and build one another up, as they were already doing. Encouragement gives strength in a discouraging world. Say the encouraging words you are thinking to someone today.

days.title: Stirring one another to love
days.summary: Hebrews calls believers to consider one another carefully and stir each other toward love and good works. This requires knowing each other well and staying close. Think of one person you can inspire toward good today.

days.title: Kindness to strangers
days.summary: Hebrews urges believers not to forget hospitality to strangers, noting that some have welcomed angels without knowing it. Kindness to strangers matters to God. Notice and welcome someone new today.

days.title: Love comes from God
days.summary: John reminds us that love comes from God, and that those who love show that they know Him. Every act of kindness and friendship springs from His love. Use this extra day to do something loving you would not otherwise have done.

days.title: Trusting with all your heart
days.summary: Proverbs calls us to trust the Lord with all our heart rather than leaning on our own limited understanding. God sees the whole picture when we see only a part. Hand Him the questions you cannot answer today and lean on Him.

days.title: A very present help
days.summary: Psalm 46 declares that God is our refuge, our strength, and a very present help in trouble. His help is near and reliable, even when everything else is shaking. Run to Him today, whatever you are facing.

days.title: Be still and know
days.summary: In the middle of chaos, God says, be still and know that I am God. Stillness means letting go of frantic striving and remembering who is in control. Take a few quiet minutes today to rest in His sovereignty.

days.title: Through the waters and the fire
days.summary: God promised His people that He would be with them through the waters and the fire. He does not promise to remove every difficulty, but He promises they will not destroy us. Trust His presence with you in whatever you are passing through.

days.title: Faith in the middle of the storm
days.summary: After calming a violent storm, Jesus asked His frightened disciples why they had no faith. Fear forgot that He was in the boat with them. Remember today that He is present in your storm.

days.title: Be of good cheer, it is I
days.summary: When the disciples saw Jesus walking on the water, they were afraid until He said, be of good cheer, it is I. Sometimes He comes to us in ways we do not first recognize. Listen for His voice in your storm today.

days.title: The hand that catches us
days.summary: When Peter began to sink, Jesus immediately reached out and caught him. Even our faltering faith is held by His strong hand. Call out to Him today if you feel yourself sinking.

days.title: When I am afraid
days.summary: David, captured and afraid, prayed that whenever he was afraid he would trust in God. Trust is often a choice we make while fear is still present. Make this verse your response whenever fear arises today.

days.title: Through the dark valley
days.summary: Psalm 23 describes walking through the valley of the shadow of death without fear, because the Shepherd is present. The valley is a passage, not a destination. Take comfort today that your Shepherd walks with you through every dark place.

days.title: Under the shadow of the Almighty
days.summary: Psalm 91 promises that those who dwell in God's secret place will rest in His shadow. To be in someone's shadow, you must stay close. Make God's presence your home today, not just a place you visit.

days.title: My refuge and my fortress
days.summary: The psalmist declares aloud that the Lord is his refuge, fortress, and God. Speaking truth strengthens faith, especially when fear is loud. Say these words today and claim God as your own refuge.

days.title: A stronghold in the day of trouble
days.summary: Nahum reminds us that the Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble. He personally knows those who trust in Him. Remember today that God is good, strong, and knows you by name.

days.title: He makes the storm a calm
days.summary: Psalm 107 describes sailors at their wits' end who cried to God, and He calmed the storm. When our own strength runs out, God is still able. Cry out to Him today, whatever storm you face.

days.title: Fear not, I am with thee
days.summary: Isaiah 41:10 tells us not to fear because God is with us and is our God. He promises to strengthen, help, and uphold us with His powerful right hand. Read it slowly today and let each phrase steady your heart.

days.title: Our God is able
days.summary: Facing a blazing furnace, three young men declared that their God was able to deliver them. They trusted God's power more than the king's threat. Stand today on the truth that God is able, whatever you are facing.

days.title: Faithful even if not
days.summary: The three young men said that even if God did not deliver them, they still would not bow to the idol. Their faith did not depend on a specific outcome. Pray boldly today, and settle in your heart to trust God even if not.

days.title: Joy when the fields fail
days.summary: Habakkuk imagined every crop failing and every stall empty, yet he chose to rejoice in the Lord. His joy came from God, not from his circumstances. Name what is failing in your life today, and then choose to rejoice in God anyway.

days.title: Trust that holds on
days.summary: In the depths of loss and confusion, Job declared that he would trust God even if God slew him. His trust was anchored in God's character, not his circumstances. Tell God your honest questions today and still choose to hold on to Him.

days.title: Our eyes are upon thee
days.summary: Facing a vast army, King Jehoshaphat admitted he had no power and no plan, but said his eyes were on God. Admitting our limits frees us to look to Him. Pray this honest prayer today and fix your eyes on God.

days.title: The battle belongs to God
days.summary: God told King Jehoshaphat not to fear the great army, because the battle was not his but God's. Judah praised God, and He gave them victory. Hand over the battle you have been carrying and trust God with it today.

days.title: Stand still and see
days.summary: Trapped between the sea and Pharaoh's army, the Israelites were told to stand still and see God's salvation. God then parted the sea. When you feel trapped today, stop panicking and watch for God to make a way.

days.title: The Lord fights for you
days.summary: Moses promised the fearful Israelites that the Lord would fight for them and they could be still. God steps in on behalf of His people. Rest today in His promise to fight for you.

days.title: The Lord is on my side
days.summary: The psalmist declared that because the Lord was on his side, he would not fear what people could do. Human opposition cannot undo God's love or promises. Let go today of the fear of what others think or do.

days.title: All things working together
days.summary: Romans 8:28 promises that God works all things together for good for those who love Him. It does not say all things are good, but that God weaves even hard things into His purpose. Trust today that nothing is wasted in His hands.

days.title: If God be for us
days.summary: Paul asks, if God is for us, who can be against us? God proved He is for us by giving His own Son. When you feel outnumbered today, remember that God is on your side.

days.title: More with us than against us
days.summary: When Elisha's servant saw an enemy army surrounding them, Elisha said those with them were more than those against them. God opened the servant's eyes to see His invisible army. Ask God to open your eyes to His presence around you today.

days.title: My help comes from the Lord
days.summary: Pilgrims singing Psalm 121 declared that their help came from the Lord who made heaven and earth. Nothing is beyond the power of the Creator. Look past every lesser source of help and look to Him today.

days.title: Blessed is the one who trusts
days.summary: Jeremiah contrasts those who trust in people with those who trust in the Lord and make Him their hope. Those who rely ultimately on anything else end up dry. Make God your trust and your hope today.

days.title: Roots by the river
days.summary: Jeremiah pictures the person who trusts God as a tree planted by a river, green and fruitful even in drought. Trust does not remove hard seasons, but it keeps us alive through them. Push your roots deeper into God today.

days.title: A heart that is not troubled
days.summary: Jesus told His confused and fearful disciples not to let their hearts be troubled but to believe in God and in Him. A troubled heart is calmed by turning our trust to the One in control. Name what troubles you today and bring it to Jesus.

days.title: Trusting in the name of the Lord
days.summary: David observed that some trust in chariots and horses, but he chose to trust in the name of the Lord. Everyone trusts in something, and only God never fails. Consider where your confidence rests today and place it in Him.

days.title: As far as the east from the west
days.summary: David wrote that God removes our sins as far as the east is from the west, a distance that can never be measured. Forgiven sins do not need to be carried again. Receive God's forgiveness fully today and let removed sins stay removed.

days.title: The joy of being forgiven
days.summary: David, who knew the weight of hidden sin, declared that the one whose sin is forgiven and covered is truly blessed. Real happiness comes not from never failing but from being forgiven. Bring anything hidden to God today and find the joy of forgiveness.

days.title: Confession that brings freedom
days.summary: David found freedom when he stopped hiding his sin and confessed it to the Lord. Confession is agreeing honestly with God, and it ends the exhausting work of hiding. Bring anything you have been hiding to Him today.

days.title: White as snow
days.summary: Through Isaiah, God invited His wayward people to come and reason with Him, promising to make scarlet sins white as snow. We cannot remove sin's stain, but God can. Accept His invitation to come as you are today.

days.title: God delights in mercy
days.summary: Micah marvels that no god is like the true God, who pardons sin and does not hold on to anger. God forgives not reluctantly but because He delights in mercy. Come to Him today, knowing He is glad to forgive.

days.title: Sins cast into the sea
days.summary: Micah promises that God will turn to us with compassion, subdue our sins, and cast them into the depths of the sea. Forgiven sins are gone for good, beyond reach. Do not go looking for what God has buried; leave it there today.

days.title: Forgiven and forgiving
days.summary: In teaching His disciples to pray, Jesus tied our forgiveness from God to our forgiveness of others. A heart that receives mercy becomes merciful. Ask God today for grace to release a debt someone owes you.

days.title: A forgiving heart
days.summary: Jesus emphasized that those who forgive others will be forgiven by their heavenly Father. Unforgiveness shows we have not grasped our own forgiveness, and it harms us too. Take one step toward forgiving someone today.

days.title: How often should I forgive
days.summary: Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive a brother, suggesting seven times as generous. Like Peter, we often want to know where forgiveness can stop. Bring your own count of offences to Jesus today.

days.title: Seventy times seven
days.summary: Jesus answered Peter by saying forgiveness should reach seventy times seven, which means we should stop counting. When we grasp how much God has forgiven us, our grievances look different. Put away your scorecard today.

days.title: Judge not, forgive freely
days.summary: Jesus told His followers not to judge or condemn but to forgive, because the measure we use for others comes back to us. A critical spirit tends to return on us, while mercy multiplies. Choose mercy over judgment today.

days.title: The father who runs
days.summary: When the prodigal son came home, his father saw him from far away, ran to him, and embraced him. Jesus told this story to show God's eagerness to welcome sinners. If you have wandered, take a step toward home today.

days.title: Lost and found again
days.summary: The father celebrated his returning son, saying he was lost and is found, though the older brother resented it. God rejoices over every person who comes home. Celebrate grace shown to others today, and remember that heaven rejoices over you too.

days.title: God meant it for good
days.summary: Joseph told his brothers that what they meant for evil, God meant for good to save many lives. Seeing God's purpose allowed Joseph to forgive rather than take revenge. Trust God today to bring good out of the wrongs done to you.

days.title: Joseph forgives his brothers
days.summary: When Joseph revealed himself to his brothers, he told them not to be grieved or angry with themselves, because God had sent him ahead to preserve life. His forgiveness sought their healing, not just their release. Ask God today for a heart that forgives like Joseph.

days.title: Brothers embrace again
days.summary: After twenty years of separation, Jacob feared meeting the brother he had wronged, but Esau ran to embrace him. God had softened both their hearts. Pray today for a broken relationship in your life; God can bring reconciliation.

days.title: First be reconciled
days.summary: Jesus taught that if someone has something against us, we should leave our offering and first be reconciled. Our relationship with God is connected to our relationships with others. Take the first step toward making peace with someone today.

days.title: Putting away bitterness
days.summary: Paul urges us to put away bitterness, anger, quarrelling, harsh words, and malice. These often start with an unhealed hurt and grow over time. Ask God today to show you any root of bitterness and help you put it away.

days.title: Forgiving as Christ forgave
days.summary: Paul calls us to forgive others in the same way Christ forgave us, completely, freely, and at great cost. We can only give the forgiveness we have received. When forgiving feels impossible, start by remembering how Christ forgave you.

days.title: Repaying no one evil for evil
days.summary: Paul tells us not to repay evil for evil, but to live honourably before everyone. Revenge only adds harm and keeps the cycle going. Trust God to make things right, and choose to do what is good today.

days.title: Living peaceably with all
days.summary: Paul urges us to live peaceably with everyone as far as it depends on us. We are not responsible for others' choices, but we must do our part. Ask what lies in you to do for peace today, and leave the rest with God.

days.title: Overcoming evil with good
days.summary: Paul tells us not to be overcome by evil but to overcome evil with good. Responding to cruelty with kindness disarms hostility and reflects God's heart. Look for a way to do good to someone who has wronged you today.

days.title: The glory of overlooking an offence
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that a wise person is slow to anger and finds glory in overlooking an offence. Not every small wrong needs to be confronted. Choose today to let a minor offence pass.

days.title: Love covers wrongs
days.summary: Proverbs contrasts hatred, which stirs up conflict, with love, which covers wrongs. Love protects others rather than exposing every failure. Choose words today that cover with grace instead of stirring up strife.

days.title: The ministry of reconciliation
days.summary: Paul explains that God reconciled us to Himself through Christ and then gave us the ministry of reconciliation. Every believer becomes a messenger of peace. Look for an opportunity to help bring peace today.

days.title: God reconciling the world
days.summary: Paul declares that God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not counting their trespasses against them. Our sin was placed on Christ, and His righteousness on us. Receive this good news today and share it with someone.

days.title: Loved while still sinners
days.summary: Paul writes that God proved His love by sending Christ to die for us while we were still sinners. His love was not a reward for goodness but a gift to the undeserving. Rest today in a love that does not depend on your performance.

days.title: Reconciled to God
days.summary: Paul argues that if God reconciled us when we were His enemies, He will much more keep us now that we are His. Our security rests on His commitment, not our ability. Let this truth calm your fears today.

days.title: Welcoming back a brother
days.summary: Paul asked Philemon to receive his runaway slave Onesimus as he would receive Paul himself, and offered to pay his debt. This pictures how Christ stands in our place before the Father. Be a peacemaker or a welcoming heart for someone today.

days.title: Sins remembered no more
days.summary: God promises to be merciful to our unrighteousness and to remember our sins no more. He chooses never to bring forgiven sin up again. End this month by resting in that promise and walking in the freedom He gives.

days.title: A lamp unto my feet
days.summary: The psalmist compares God's Word to a lamp that lights the next step on a dark path. It does not always show the whole road, but it gives enough light to walk faithfully. Open God's Word today and let it show you your next step.

days.title: The Word hidden in the heart
days.summary: The psalmist hid God's Word in his heart so that he would not sin against God. Scripture stored in the heart rises up to protect us when temptation comes. Choose a verse today and begin memorizing it.

days.title: Meditating day and night
days.summary: As Joshua prepared to lead Israel, God told him to meditate on His Word day and night and obey it. True success flows from a life shaped by Scripture. Start today's challenges by letting God's Word fill your mind.

days.title: Delight in God's law
days.summary: Psalm 1 describes the blessed person as one who delights in God's law and meditates on it day and night. When we love God's Word, our minds return to it often. Ask God to grow your delight in Scripture today.

days.title: A tree planted by the rivers
days.summary: Psalm 1 compares the person who delights in God's Word to a tree planted by rivers, bearing fruit in season and never withering. Growth comes gradually as we stay rooted in Scripture. Keep your roots in His Word today and trust Him for fruit in season.

days.title: All Scripture given by God
days.summary: Paul reminded Timothy that all Scripture is breathed out by God and useful for teaching, reproof, correction, and training in righteousness. Scripture is given not only to inform us but to transform us. Approach your Bible today knowing God breathed it.

days.title: The living and powerful Word
days.summary: Hebrews describes God's Word as living, powerful, and sharper than any sword, discerning the thoughts and intents of the heart. Scripture reads us even as we read it. Come to it today expecting it to speak and search your heart.

days.title: The Word that stands for ever
days.summary: Isaiah contrasts fading grass and flowers with the eternal Word of God. Human glory passes, but God's Word stands for ever. Anchor yourself today in the Word that never changes.

days.title: Living by every word
days.summary: When tempted in the wilderness, Jesus answered that people live not by bread alone but by every word from God. Our souls need daily nourishment from Scripture. Make sure your soul is fed by God's Word today.

days.title: Doers of the Word
days.summary: James warns that hearing God's Word without doing it is self-deception. Knowledge without obedience leaves us unchanged. Act on something God has shown you in His Word today.

days.title: Why call Him Lord
days.summary: Jesus asked why people called Him Lord but did not do what He said. Calling Him Lord means letting Him direct our everyday choices. Let His question search you today, and bring your actions into line with your words.

days.title: Building on the rock
days.summary: Jesus compared those who hear and obey His words to a wise man who built his house on a rock. Storms come to everyone, but obedience provides a foundation that holds. Build your life today on hearing and doing His words.

days.title: Love that obeys
days.summary: Jesus told His disciples that if they loved Him, they would keep His commandments. Obedience flows from love, not fear, and love shows itself in obedience. Spend time with Jesus today and let your love for Him shape how you live.

days.title: To obey is better
days.summary: When Saul kept what God told him to destroy and claimed it was for sacrifice, Samuel said that obedience is better than sacrifice. Religious gestures cannot replace a listening, obedient heart. Do what God has asked of you today.

days.title: God's words upon your heart
days.summary: Moses told Israel that God's words should be in their hearts, not only on stone or paper. When His Word lives within us, it shapes our desires and decisions. Carry one verse with you today and let it settle deep in your heart.

days.title: Teaching the Word at home
days.summary: Moses told parents to teach God's words diligently and to talk about them at home, on the road, at bedtime, and in the morning. Faith is often passed on best through everyday conversation. Look for ordinary moments to talk about God today.

days.title: The Word that restores the soul
days.summary: David wrote that God's law is perfect, restoring the soul and making wise the simple. Scripture brings life to weary hearts and wisdom to anyone with an open heart. Go to God's Word today and let it restore your soul.

days.title: Sweeter than honey
days.summary: David declared that God's words are more precious than fine gold and sweeter than honey. He had found a treasure and delight in Scripture beyond anything else. Ask God for a taste for His Word, and savour it slowly today.

days.title: Eyes opened to wonders
days.summary: The psalmist asked God to open his eyes to see wondrous things in His Word. We need God's help to see what is there, and Scripture is full of marvels. Pray this prayer before reading today and read with expectation.

days.title: Light from God's words
days.summary: The psalmist wrote that the entrance of God's words brings light and gives understanding to the simple. When Scripture enters our hearts, confusion clears. Let God's Word into whatever feels unclear in your life today.

days.title: Words found and eaten
days.summary: Jeremiah, though persecuted, found God's words and ate them, and they became the joy of his heart. Joy can come through feeding on Scripture even in hardship. Take in God's Word deeply today and let it become your joy.

days.title: Searching the Scriptures daily
days.summary: The Bereans received Paul's message eagerly and searched the Scriptures daily to confirm it. Openness and discernment belong together. Listen eagerly today, and test what you hear against God's Word.

days.title: Scriptures that point to Jesus
days.summary: Jesus told religious leaders that the Scriptures they studied testified of Him, yet they did not come to Him. The goal of Bible reading is not just knowledge but knowing Christ. Look for Jesus as you read God's Word today.

days.title: Faith comes by hearing
days.summary: Paul explains that faith comes by hearing the word of God. Faith is not manufactured by effort but built by exposure to God's truth. If your faith feels weak, feed on His Word today, and share it with someone else.

days.title: Rightly handling the Word
days.summary: Paul urged Timothy to be diligent in handling God's Word accurately, like a skilled workman. Understanding Scripture well takes effort and care. Read carefully today, seeking what God actually means.

days.title: A heart prepared to learn and teach
days.summary: Ezra prepared his heart to seek God's law, to obey it, and then to teach it. What we teach must first be lived. Follow Ezra's order today: seek, do, and then teach.

days.title: Reading with understanding
days.summary: When Ezra read God's law to the people, the Levites explained it so they could understand it. Understanding, not just hearing, changes lives. Seek understanding when Scripture confuses you, and help others understand it too.

days.title: Abram goes as God said
days.summary: Abram left everything familiar and departed as the Lord had spoken, at seventy-five years old. Age is no barrier to obedience. Respond today to whatever God is asking, whatever stage of life you are in.

days.title: Obeying without seeing the road
days.summary: Hebrews highlights that Abraham obeyed God's call and went out not knowing where he was going. Faith often means stepping forward without seeing the end. Trust the One who leads you today, even when the road is unclear.

days.title: Whatsoever He says
days.summary: At the wedding in Cana, Mary told the servants to do whatever Jesus said, and their obedience led to His first miracle. Bring your problems to Jesus and then obey Him, even when it seems strange. Whatever He tells you today, do it.

days.title: Nevertheless at thy word
days.summary: After a fruitless night of fishing, Peter obeyed Jesus anyway, saying, nevertheless at thy word, and caught a huge haul. Obedience sometimes means acting against our own experience and weariness. When Jesus speaks, say nevertheless and obey.

days.title: Joy in the middle of trials
days.summary: James tells believers to count it all joy when they face various trials. This is not pretending pain away, but choosing to see trials from God's perspective. Ask God to help you see your current trial through His eyes.

days.title: Trials that build endurance
days.summary: James explains that the testing of our faith produces endurance. Like muscles strengthened by resistance, faith grows stronger through trials. Remember today that your season of testing is not wasted.

days.title: The crown of life
days.summary: James promises the crown of life to those who endure trials out of love for God. Endurance is love holding on through difficulty. Keep holding on today, knowing God sees and will reward your faithfulness.

days.title: A way of escape
days.summary: Paul reminds us that our temptations are common to everyone and that God faithfully limits them and provides a way of escape. Temptation is never stronger than God's grace. Look for the way out God provides and take it today.

days.title: The whole armour of God
days.summary: Paul urged believers to put on the whole armour of God to stand against the devil's schemes. The armour is God's provision, and our part is to put it on. Clothe yourself in His truth, faith, and Word before facing today's battles.

days.title: Having done all, stand
days.summary: Paul urges believers to take up God's armour so that, having done all, they can still stand in the evil day. Sometimes victory simply means not giving up ground. If you have done all you can, keep standing today.

days.title: Standing fast in the faith
days.summary: Paul urged the Corinthians to watch, stand firm in the faith, act with courage, and be strong. They faced many pressures, as we do today. Be alert and steady today, and let everything you do be done in love.

days.title: Glory in tribulation
days.summary: Paul says believers can glory even in tribulations, because tribulation produces endurance, character, and hope. God uses hard times to build lasting strength. Trust that He is at work in your trouble today.

days.title: Hope that does not disappoint
days.summary: Paul writes that hope in God does not disappoint, because His love has been poured into our hearts by the Holy Ghost. Our hope rests not on circumstances but on God's love already given. Anchor your hope in His love today.

days.title: Pressed but not crushed
days.summary: Paul admitted he was troubled on every side and perplexed, yet not crushed and not in despair. God's power works through fragile people. If you feel pressed today, trust that His strength will keep you from being crushed.

days.title: Light affliction, lasting glory
days.summary: Paul called his many sufferings a light and momentary affliction compared to the eternal weight of glory to come. Perspective changes how we carry our trials. Set your trouble on the scale with eternity today.

days.title: Grace that is sufficient
days.summary: When Paul asked God to remove his thorn, God answered that His grace was sufficient and His strength is made perfect in weakness. Not every hardship is removed, but grace is always enough. Rest today in grace that is sufficient for whatever remains.

days.title: Not surprised by trials
days.summary: Peter told suffering believers not to be surprised by fiery trials, as though something strange were happening. Trials are a normal part of following Christ, not a sign that God has forgotten us. Meet today's difficulties with a steady heart, knowing you are still beloved.

days.title: Faith tried by fire
days.summary: Peter compares the testing of faith to gold refined by fire, saying faith is more precious than gold. Trials burn away what is false and reveal genuine faith. Trust the Refiner today, knowing your tested faith will bring glory to God.

days.title: Coming forth as gold
days.summary: Though Job could not find God, he trusted that God knew his way and that he would come forth from the trial as gold. God sees every step even when we cannot see Him. Trust today that your trial has an end and a purpose.

days.title: Many troubles, one Deliverer
days.summary: David wrote that the righteous face many afflictions, but the Lord delivers them out of them all. Following God does not exempt us from trouble, but no trouble has the final word. Count on your Deliverer today, whatever you are facing.

days.title: Lessons learned in affliction
days.summary: The psalmist looked back and said it was good that he had been afflicted, because it taught him God's ways. Hard seasons often teach us lessons comfort never could. Thank God today for what He has taught you through difficulty.

days.title: Jesus has overcome the world
days.summary: Jesus told His disciples they would have tribulation in the world, but they could have peace in Him because He has overcome the world. Trouble is certain, but so is His victory. Take heart today in the One who has already overcome.

days.title: Running the race with patience
days.summary: Hebrews encourages us, surrounded by a cloud of faithful witnesses, to lay aside every weight and sin and run our race with endurance. The Christian life is a marathon, not a sprint. Ask God to show you what is slowing you down, and lay it aside today.

days.title: Looking unto Jesus
days.summary: Hebrews tells us to run looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith, who endured the cross for the joy set before Him. He is both our example and our goal. Keep your eyes on Jesus today.

days.title: Strength for the weary mind
days.summary: Hebrews tells weary believers to consider Jesus, who endured great hostility, so that they would not grow faint in their minds. Reflecting on His endurance gives us fresh courage. When you feel worn down today, stop and consider Him.

days.title: Not weary in well doing
days.summary: Paul encourages believers not to grow weary in doing good, because in due season they will reap if they do not give up. Good done in faith is never wasted. Keep planting today; the harvest will come in God's season.

days.title: Rising up on wings
days.summary: Isaiah promises fresh strength to everyone who waits upon the Lord: soaring like eagles, running without weariness, and walking without fainting. Waiting on God means exchanging our weakness for His strength. Bring Him your tiredness today.

days.title: Strong and of good courage
days.summary: As Joshua faced a daunting task, God commanded him to be strong and courageous because He would be with him wherever he went. Courage is a choice we make because of God's presence. Choose courage today, knowing He goes with you.

days.title: He will not fail you
days.summary: Moses told Israel to be strong and courageous because the Lord goes with them and will not fail or forsake them. People and plans may fail, but God never will. Hold on to His promise of faithful presence today.

days.title: Courage for those who hope
days.summary: After a season of deep distress, David encouraged all who hope in the Lord to take courage, promising that God would strengthen their hearts. We take a small step of courage, and God supplies the strength. Take heart today if your hope is in Him.

days.title: In the name of the Lord
days.summary: Facing Goliath with only a sling, David declared that he came in the name of the Lord of hosts. His confidence was in God's power, not his weapons. Face your giants today in the name of the Lord.

days.title: Encouraged in the Lord
days.summary: When David returned to find his town burned and his men turning against him, he encouraged himself in the Lord his God. When no one else encourages us, we can find strength in God. Turn to Him today and remember His faithfulness.

days.title: Faithful as before
days.summary: When a law forbade prayer to God, Daniel kept praying three times a day as he always had. His courage under pressure grew from years of faithful habit. Build steady habits of prayer today that will hold you in times of testing.

days.title: Finishing the course
days.summary: From prison, near the end of his life, Paul said he had fought a good fight, finished his course, and kept the faith. Standing firm leads not to an easy life but to a finished one. Keep fighting, running, and believing today.

days.title: The joy of the Lord is strength
days.summary: When the people wept over God's law, Nehemiah told them to rejoice, because the joy of the Lord is their strength. Joy rooted in God gives energy, courage, and resilience. Let God's joy become your strength today.

days.title: Fulness of joy
days.summary: David declared that in God's presence is fulness of joy and at His right hand are pleasures for evermore. Earthly joys are gifts, but only God can satisfy completely. Spend time in His presence today and find full joy.

days.title: Serving with gladness
days.summary: Psalm 100 tells us to serve the Lord with gladness and come before Him with singing. We serve a good God out of gratitude, not fear. Do your work today gladly, as service to the Lord.

days.title: Entering His gates with praise
days.summary: Psalm 100 invites us to enter God's gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise. Gratitude opens our hearts and shrinks our worries. Before you ask for anything today, begin by thanking and praising Him.

days.title: This is the day
days.summary: Psalm 118 celebrates God's rescue and declares that this is the day the Lord has made. Every day belongs to Him, not just the easy ones. Choose to rejoice today, recognizing whose day it is.

days.title: Rejoice in the Lord always
days.summary: Writing from prison, Paul told the Philippians to rejoice in the Lord always, and repeated it for emphasis. Joy in the Lord does not depend on circumstances but on who He is. Choose to rejoice in Him today, whatever your situation.

days.title: Rejoice evermore
days.summary: Paul's short command to rejoice evermore calls for a steady undercurrent of gladness in every part of life. This joy comes from remembering who God is, not from easy circumstances. Return to joy again and again throughout today.

days.title: Praise that never stops
days.summary: After a frightening escape, David decided to bless the Lord at all times and keep His praise continually in his mouth. Praise can become a habit that shapes how we see everything. Make praise your constant response today.

days.title: Magnifying the Lord together
days.summary: David invited others to magnify the Lord with him and exalt His name together. Shared praise strengthens faith and multiplies joy. Share something God has done with someone today and praise Him together.

days.title: A joyful noise
days.summary: Psalm 95 invites us to sing and make a joyful noise to the Rock of our salvation. God delights in glad hearts, not perfect voices. Sing to the Lord today, wherever you are.

days.title: Kneeling before our Maker
days.summary: Psalm 95 moves from joyful singing to quiet reverence, inviting us to bow and kneel before the Lord our Maker. Bowing acknowledges His greatness and releases our need for control. Take a quiet moment today to bow your heart before Him.

days.title: The beauty of holiness
days.summary: Psalm 96 calls us to worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness. God's holiness is His radiant goodness, and it draws us to worship with awe. Reflect on His holiness today and let its beauty move your heart.

days.title: Bless the Lord, O my soul
days.summary: David commanded his own soul to bless the Lord with all that was within him. Sometimes our souls need to be told to praise, and feelings often follow. Speak to your soul today and bring all of yourself into worship.

days.title: Forget not His benefits
days.summary: David told his soul to bless the Lord and forget not all His benefits, then listed God's forgiveness, healing, redemption, and mercy. Forgetfulness is an enemy of praise. Make a list of God's blessings today and thank Him for each one.

days.title: Everything that has breath
days.summary: The book of Psalms ends with a call for everything that has breath to praise the Lord. Every breath is God's gift and a reason to worship Him. Take a deep breath today and use it to praise Him.

days.title: Worship in spirit and truth
days.summary: Jesus told the Samaritan woman that true worship is not about location but about worshipping God in spirit and in truth. Worship needs both genuine heart engagement and truth about who God is. Worship Him today wherever you are, with heart and mind.

days.title: Joy that is full
days.summary: Jesus told His disciples He had spoken to them so that His joy might remain in them and their joy might be full. His joy came from His union with the Father, and He offers it to us. Abide in Him today and let His joy fill you.

days.title: Filled with joy and peace
days.summary: Paul prayed that the God of hope would fill believers with joy and peace in believing, so they would overflow with hope. Joy and peace are gifts God pours in as we trust Him. Ask Him to fill you today and renew your trust in Him.

days.title: Joy comes in the morning
days.summary: David wrote that weeping may last for a night, but joy comes in the morning. Seasons of sorrow are real, but they are not permanent for God's people. Hold on today if you are in a night season; morning is coming.

days.title: Great things God has done
days.summary: The returning exiles in Psalm 126 declared that the Lord had done great things for them, and they were glad. Joy flows from remembering God's works. Name the great things God has done for you today and rejoice.

days.title: Sowing in tears, reaping in joy
days.summary: Psalm 126 promises that those who sow in tears will reap in joy. Faithful work done through sorrow will bring a harvest. Keep sowing in faith today, even if you are weeping.

days.title: The garment of praise
days.summary: Isaiah describes God giving beauty for ashes, joy for mourning, and a garment of praise for a heavy spirit. Jesus fulfilled this mission and still makes these exchanges. Bring Him your heaviness today and put on praise.

days.title: God my strength and my song
days.summary: Isaiah's song declares that God is salvation, strength, and song, and so we can trust and not be afraid. He gives power to endure and joy to celebrate. Make this verse your song today.

days.title: A song of deliverance
days.summary: After crossing the Red Sea, Israel sang the first recorded song in the Bible, praising God as their strength, song, and salvation. Praise is the natural response to God's rescue. Let the memory of His deliverance turn into a song today.

days.title: Worship with all your might
days.summary: When the ark came to Jerusalem, David danced before the Lord with all his might, unconcerned about how he looked. Wholehearted worship does not hold back for fear of others' opinions. Give God your whole heart in worship today.

days.title: A new song
days.summary: After God lifted David out of the pit, He put a new song of praise in his mouth, and many who saw it came to trust the Lord. Our praise is a witness that can stir others' faith. Share your story of God's faithfulness today.

days.title: Lovingkindness better than life
days.summary: In a dry wilderness, David declared that God's lovingkindness is better than life itself. Recognizing the greatness of His love leads naturally to praise. Reflect on God's faithful love today and let it move you to worship.

days.title: Joy in heaven
days.summary: Jesus said there is joy in the presence of God's angels over one sinner who repents. Heaven celebrates every return, showing God's glad welcome. Share in that joy today by praying for the lost and celebrating every return.

days.title: God rejoices over you
days.summary: Zephaniah describes God in the midst of His people, mighty to save, rejoicing over them with joy and singing. God does not merely tolerate His people; He delights in them. Let the truth that God rejoices over you sink in today.

days.title: A good thing to give thanks
days.summary: Psalm 92 declares that it is good to give thanks to the Lord, declaring His love in the morning and His faithfulness at night. Gratitude is good for God, for us, and for others. Begin and end your day with thanks today.

days.title: Thou art worthy
days.summary: In heaven's throne room, the elders cast their crowns before God and declare He is worthy because He created all things. Worship is the eternal activity of heaven, and our praise now is practice for it. Tell God today that He is worthy.

days.title: More blessed to give
days.summary: Paul reminded the Ephesian leaders of Jesus' words that it is more blessed to give than to receive. Real blessing is found not in getting more but in giving, especially to the weak. Discover the joy of giving in some way today.

days.title: A cheerful giver
days.summary: Paul taught that each person should give as they decide in their heart, not grudgingly or under pressure, because God loves a cheerful giver. God cares more about the heart than the size of the gift. Give gladly today, remembering how generous He has been to you.

days.title: Sowing generously
days.summary: Paul compares generosity to sowing seed: those who sow sparingly reap sparingly, and those who sow bountifully reap bountifully. The harvest includes grace, joy, and the ability to give more. Sow generously today with your time, kindness, and resources.

days.title: Give, and it shall be given
days.summary: Jesus described giving that returns in overflowing measure, pressed down and running over, and said the measure we use will be measured back to us. This applies to mercy and kindness as well as money. Be generous in every way today.

days.title: The generous soul refreshed
days.summary: Proverbs promises that the generous person will prosper, and the one who waters others will be watered too. Refreshing others often refreshes us. If you feel dry today, try encouraging or helping someone else.

days.title: Lending to the Lord
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that showing pity to the poor is lending to the Lord, and He will repay. God takes our kindness to the needy personally. Show compassion to someone in need today, knowing it is never wasted.

days.title: Honouring God with what you have
days.summary: Proverbs calls us to honour the Lord with our substance and the firstfruits of our increase. Giving God the first and best, not the leftovers, is a statement of trust. Consider today how you can honour God with your best.

days.title: Withholding no good thing
days.summary: Proverbs warns against withholding good from those to whom it is due when we have the power to do it. Delay is a quiet way of withholding. Do the good you have been meaning to do today.

days.title: The windows of heaven
days.summary: When God's people held back their giving, He challenged them to prove Him and see if He would not pour out an overflowing blessing. Generosity is ultimately a matter of trusting God to provide. Trust Him with your giving today.

days.title: The widow's two mites
days.summary: Jesus said a poor widow's two small coins were more than all the large gifts, because she gave all she had. God measures gifts by sacrifice and heart, not size. Give what you can today with your whole heart.

days.title: Giving in secret
days.summary: Jesus taught His followers to give so quietly that the left hand does not know what the right hand is doing. Giving to be seen receives only human applause, but secret giving is rewarded by God. Do something generous in secret today.

days.title: Let your light shine
days.summary: Jesus told His followers to let their light shine so others would see their good works and glorify the Father. Our lives should point people to God, not to ourselves. Let your light shine through ordinary good works today, and give Him the glory.

days.title: Unto the least of these
days.summary: Jesus said that whatever we do for the least of His brethren, we do for Him. He identifies with the hungry, the stranger, the sick, and the prisoner. Look for someone in need today and serve them as if serving Christ.

days.title: A cup of cold water
days.summary: Jesus said that even giving a cup of cold water to one of His little ones will not lose its reward. God notices the smallest kindnesses. Look for a simple way to show kindness today.

days.title: Created for good works
days.summary: Paul writes that we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works that He prepared in advance. We are not saved by good works, but for them. Ask God today to show you the good works He has prepared for you.

days.title: Careful to do good
days.summary: Paul told Titus that those who believe in God should be careful to maintain good works, which are good and profitable for others. Good works need thought and intention. Think ahead today about how you can bless someone, and follow through.

days.title: A pattern of good works
days.summary: Paul urged Titus to be a pattern of good works in all things, a model others could follow. Every one of us is an example to someone. Live today in a way you would be glad for others to copy.

days.title: Doing good to all
days.summary: Paul urges us to do good to all people as we have opportunity, especially to fellow believers. Opportunities to do good are valuable and do not last forever. Watch for chances to do good today and take them.

days.title: Sacrifices that please God
days.summary: Hebrews says that doing good and sharing with others are sacrifices that please God. They cost us something, and it is easy to forget them. Remember today to offer God a sacrifice of goodness and generosity.

days.title: Hope not in riches
days.summary: Paul told Timothy to warn the rich not to be proud or trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God who richly gives us all things to enjoy. Wealth is not evil, but it makes a poor foundation. Keep your trust in the Giver, not the gifts, today.

days.title: Rich in good works
days.summary: Paul urged wealthy believers to be rich in good works, ready to give and willing to share. Generosity builds treasure that lasts beyond this life. Whatever your finances, seek to be rich in good works today.

days.title: Light rising in the darkness
days.summary: God told His people that if they poured themselves out for the hungry and afflicted, their light would rise in the darkness. Serving others often lifts our own gloom. Look for someone to help today, and let God bring light to you as you do.

days.title: An open hand to the poor
days.summary: Moses acknowledged that the poor would always be in the land, and therefore commanded God's people to open their hands wide to the needy. The size of the problem is no excuse for closing our hands. Open your hand to someone in need near you today.

days.title: Go and do likewise
days.summary: After telling the story of the good Samaritan, Jesus told the lawyer to go and do likewise. The question is not who deserves our love, but whether we will be a neighbour to whoever needs us. Go and show mercy to someone in need today.

days.title: Dorcas, full of good works
days.summary: Dorcas was known for being full of good works, especially making clothes for widows in need. She used a simple skill to bless many, and her life led others to faith. Use your own skills to bless someone today.

days.title: One heart and open hands
days.summary: The early believers were of one heart and soul, holding their possessions loosely and sharing so that no one lacked. Generosity flows naturally from love and unity. Consider how you could share what you have with someone in need today.

days.title: He became poor for us
days.summary: Paul pointed to Jesus, who though rich became poor for our sakes so that we might become rich. Christian generosity flows from gratitude for what Christ gave up for us. Reflect on His generosity today and let it inspire yours.

days.title: The widow's flour that lasted
days.summary: During a famine, a widow gave her last bit of food to Elijah, and God made her flour and oil last for many days. Generosity sometimes means giving from scarcity, trusting God to provide. Remember today that God can stretch whatever you offer.

days.title: A bountiful eye
days.summary: Proverbs blesses the person with a bountiful eye who gives bread to the poor. Generosity begins with seeing others' needs with kindness. Ask God today to help you see people as He sees them.

days.title: Life is more than possessions
days.summary: Jesus warned against covetousness, saying that life does not consist in the abundance of possessions. The constant desire for more can creep into any heart. Take an honest look at your desires today and let go of covetousness.

days.title: Where your treasure is
days.summary: Jesus said that where our treasure is, our heart will be also. Generosity not only flows from a changed heart but also helps change it. Look honestly at where your treasure is today and invest it where you want your heart to be.

days.title: Wait on the Lord
days.summary: David urges us twice to wait on the Lord and promises that God will strengthen our hearts as we take courage. Waiting takes courage, and God meets us with strength. Whatever you are waiting for today, wait on the Lord.

days.title: Resting and waiting patiently
days.summary: David told those frustrated by the success of the wicked to rest in the Lord and wait patiently instead of fretting. Fretting drains us, but resting in God restores peace. Bring whatever is making you fret to God today and rest in Him.

days.title: God bends down to hear
days.summary: David waited patiently for the Lord, and God bent down to hear his cry. Even long waiting does not mean God is distant. Keep crying out to Him today; He will lean in to hear you.

days.title: Good to those who wait
days.summary: In the middle of grief, Jeremiah declared that the Lord is good to those who wait for Him and seek Him. We often discover God's goodness most deeply while waiting. Seek Him today as you wait, and find Him good.

days.title: Hoping quietly
days.summary: Jeremiah says it is good both to hope and to wait quietly for the Lord's salvation. Quiet waiting is calm trust, not frantic demanding. Practice quiet, hopeful waiting today.

days.title: Prepared for those who wait
days.summary: Isaiah declared that no eye has seen or ear heard what God has prepared for those who wait for Him. Waiting is not wasted time but the season when God prepares. Trust today that God is preparing something good for you.

days.title: The vision will surely come
days.summary: God told Habakkuk that His vision had an appointed time and, though it seemed to tarry, it would surely come and not be late. God's plans are never forgotten, only timed in His wisdom. Hold on to His promises today and wait for His appointed time.

days.title: A time for everything
days.summary: Solomon wrote that there is a season and a time for every purpose under heaven. Life moves in seasons, and none of them last forever. Ask God what season you are in today and embrace it, trusting Him with its timing.

days.title: Beautiful in His time
days.summary: Solomon wrote that God makes everything beautiful in His time, though we cannot see His whole work from beginning to end. Our lives may look tangled now, but God is weaving something beautiful. Trust His timing today.

days.title: The patient farmer
days.summary: James points to the farmer, who waits patiently for the early and latter rain before the harvest. Some things cannot be hurried, and we must trust God for what only He can provide. Do your part faithfully today and wait patiently for His rain.

days.title: Establishing your heart
days.summary: James urges believers to be patient and establish their hearts, because the coming of the Lord draws near. An established heart stays steady when circumstances change. Anchor your heart today in the certain hope of Christ's return.

days.title: Patient in tribulation
days.summary: Paul calls believers to rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, and continue steadily in prayer. These three work together, with prayer keeping hope and patience alive. Make these three phrases your plan for today.

days.title: The fruit of the Spirit
days.summary: Paul lists longsuffering, or patience, among the fruit of the Spirit. Patience is not a natural trait but fruit that the Spirit grows over time. Stay close to God today and ask Him to grow patience in you.

days.title: Patience better than pride
days.summary: Solomon teaches that the end of a thing is better than its beginning and that patience is better than pride. Finishing well requires patience, and patience grows from humility. Let go of pride today and patiently keep going toward the end.

days.title: Slow to wrath
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that being slow to anger shows great understanding, while a hasty spirit puts folly on display. Understanding sees more of the situation before reacting. Pause before you respond to anger today and ask God for understanding.

days.title: Ruling your own spirit
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that ruling one's own spirit is greater than conquering a city. Self-control is a lasting kind of strength that many powerful people lack. Ask God today for help ruling your spirit where you most need it.

days.title: Swift to hear, slow to speak
days.summary: James urges us to be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger. Most of us do the opposite, but reversing the order brings wisdom and peace. Practise listening first in your conversations today.

days.title: The Lord is not slow
days.summary: Peter explained that God is not slow in keeping His promise but patient, not willing that any should perish. What looks like delay is actually mercy. Use the time God gives to share His love with someone today.

days.title: God's view of time
days.summary: Peter reminds us that with the Lord, one day is as a thousand years and a thousand years as one day. God is never rushed and never late. When impatience rises today, rest in His eternal perspective.

days.title: A promise kept at the set time
days.summary: After twenty-five years of waiting, Sarah bore Abraham a son at the set time God had spoken. God's timing seemed late but made His power unmistakable. Do not give up on God's promises today; His set time will come.

days.title: Years that seemed like days
days.summary: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed like only a few days because of his love for her. Love changes how we experience waiting. Ask God to deepen your love for Him so that waiting becomes devotion.

days.title: The child Hannah prayed for
days.summary: After years of grief and persistent prayer, Hannah received a son and declared that the Lord had given her what she asked. Her story is one of faithful prayer through long waiting. Keep bringing your long-held prayers to God today.

days.title: Watching for the morning
days.summary: The psalmist waited for the Lord more eagerly than watchmen wait for the morning. Like dawn after a long night, God's coming is certain. If you are in a dark season, wait for Him with eager hope.

days.title: Looking to the Lord
days.summary: Surrounded by corruption and betrayal, Micah declared that he would look to the Lord, wait for Him, and trust that God would hear. When people disappoint us, we can turn our eyes to God. Look to Him and wait for Him today.

days.title: The Lord waits to be gracious
days.summary: Isaiah reveals that the Lord waits, longing to be gracious and show mercy to His people. God is eager, not reluctant, to bless those who turn to Him. Turn to Him today; He has been waiting to be gracious to you.

days.title: Simeon waits in faith
days.summary: Simeon was a just and devout man who waited faithfully for the Messiah, and God allowed him to see the Christ before he died. His waiting was active and faithful, not idle. Live faithfully while you wait today, trusting God to keep His word.

days.title: Abraham patiently endured
days.summary: Hebrews says that Abraham, after patiently enduring, obtained the promise. God's promises are sure, but they often require patient endurance. Do not give up on God's promises today; endure patiently as Abraham did.

days.title: The need for patience
days.summary: Hebrews tells weary believers that they need patience, so that after doing God's will they will receive the promise. Patience fills the gap between obedience and reward. If you have done what God asked and are still waiting, be patient today.

days.title: Strengthened unto patience
days.summary: Paul prayed that believers would be strengthened with God's glorious power for patience, longsuffering, and joy. It takes divine strength to wait with joy rather than frustration. Pray for that strength today.

days.title: My times are in His hand
days.summary: Surrounded by enemies, David declared to God, my times are in thy hand. Every season and every answer rests in God's hand, not in chance or our own control. End this month by entrusting your times to Him.

days.title: Justice, mercy and humility
days.summary: When people asked what God required, Micah answered: do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God. God desires a life of integrity more than religious gestures. Live out these three requirements in ordinary ways today.

days.title: Walking securely in uprightness
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that those who walk with integrity walk securely, while those who take crooked paths will be exposed. Honesty brings freedom and confidence. Choose the upright path today, even where it costs you.

days.title: Integrity that guides
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that integrity guides the upright, while crookedness destroys those who practise it. A commitment to honesty makes many decisions clearer. Let integrity guide your choices today.

days.title: A legacy of integrity
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that a just person who walks in integrity leaves blessing for their children. Integrity becomes a legacy that shapes generations. Remember today that your honest choices are an investment in others' futures.

days.title: Truth spoken from the heart
days.summary: Psalm 15 describes the person who may dwell with God as one who walks uprightly and speaks the truth in their heart. Honesty begins inside, with ourselves and with God. Take time today to be completely honest with God about your heart.

days.title: Clean hands and a pure heart
days.summary: Psalm 24 describes those who may stand before God as having clean hands, a pure heart, and honest words. God cares about both our actions and our motives. Ask Him today to clean your hands and purify your heart.

days.title: A clean heart created
days.summary: After his great sin, David asked God to create a clean heart in him and renew a right spirit. He knew only God, the Creator, could make his heart new. Pray this prayer today and ask God to create something new in you.

days.title: Search me, O God
days.summary: After reflecting on how completely God knows him, David invited God to search his heart and know his thoughts. God's searching is not to condemn but to heal. Pray this brave prayer today and open your heart to His examination.

days.title: The way everlasting
days.summary: David asked God to see if there was any wicked way in him and to lead him in the way everlasting. God reveals our faults so He can lead us onto a better path. Let Him show you what needs to change today, and follow where He leads.

days.title: Words that please God
days.summary: David prayed that both the words of his mouth and the meditation of his heart would be acceptable to God. Our words reveal what grows in our hearts, and integrity means both please Him. Pray this prayer before you speak to anyone today.

days.title: The pure in heart
days.summary: Jesus said the pure in heart are blessed, for they shall see God. Purity of heart means single-minded devotion, not divided between God and the world. Ask God today to remove whatever divides your heart.

days.title: Let your yes be yes
days.summary: Jesus taught that our communication should simply be yes or no, without needing oaths to be believed. A person of integrity is reliable in their word. Keep every promise today, large and small.

days.title: Holy in all you do
days.summary: Peter urged believers to be holy in all their conduct because the God who called them is holy. Holiness reaches every part of life, not just religious moments. Invite God's holiness into an area you have kept separate from Him today.

days.title: A living sacrifice
days.summary: Paul urges believers, in view of God's mercies, to present their bodies as a living sacrifice to God. This is a daily surrender of our whole selves, the reasonable response to His mercy. Offer yourself to God again today.

days.title: Transformed, not conformed
days.summary: Paul calls us not to be pressed into the world's mould but to be transformed by the renewing of our minds. As God's truth fills our thinking, our lives change from the inside out. Feed your mind with God's Word today.

days.title: Think on these things
days.summary: Paul gives a filter for our thoughts: things that are true, honest, just, pure, lovely, of good report, virtuous, and praiseworthy. Our thoughts slowly shape our character. Run your thoughts through this filter today.

days.title: Daniel's settled purpose
days.summary: Far from home and under pressure, Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself, then acted wisely and respectfully. Integrity often begins with a decision made before temptation peaks. Settle in your heart today what you will and will not do.

days.title: Joseph says no to sin
days.summary: Tempted by his master's wife, Joseph refused, asking how he could do this great wickedness and sin against God. His integrity cost him, but God was with him. Stand firm today, remembering that every sin is ultimately against God.

days.title: Holding fast to integrity
days.summary: Under pressure from his friends to confess sins he had not committed, Job refused to let go of his integrity. He would not lie even to ease his situation. Hold fast to truth today, even when others pressure you to compromise.

days.title: A covenant with the eyes
days.summary: Job made a covenant with his eyes not to look upon a woman with lust. Purity begins with what we choose to look at. Consider what boundaries you need to set with your eyes today.

days.title: Guarding your heart
days.summary: Proverbs urges us to guard our hearts with all diligence, because everything in life flows from them. The heart is like a spring that determines everything downstream. Pay careful attention today to what you allow into your heart.

days.title: A good name
days.summary: Proverbs teaches that a good name is better than great riches and loving favour better than silver and gold. Trustworthy character is built slowly and is worth more than money. Choose character over gain today.

days.title: Lips that deal truly
days.summary: Proverbs says lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who deal truly are His delight. God takes pleasure in honest people. Aim to deal truly in every word and action today.

days.title: Speaking truth with one another
